text: A linked service is a connection definition, like a connection string — telling Data Factory how to reach a specific data store or compute resource. It's genuinely the foundation everything else in this entire chapter builds directly on top of.

Here's exactly where it fits. A pipeline groups activities together. Activities read and write datasets. And datasets point straight into linked services. Everything you build eventually traces back to one real connection, sitting at the bottom of that chain.

You create a linked service exactly once per data store, and reuse it across as many datasets and pipelines as you actually need — open the Manage hub, select Linked services, and select New. Every linked service you've ever built lives right here on this one page.

Selecting New opens a searchable gallery of every supported connector — hundreds of them, from Azure Blob Storage to Amazon S3 to SQL Server. Search or browse to find the one you need, then configure its specific connection details. Lessons 7 and 8 walk through two of the most common ones hands-on.

Underneath that friendly UI, every linked service is really just JSON with four real parts. Name, referenced everywhere else. Type, which connector it actually is. Type properties, the connection details specific to that type. And connect via, which integration runtime executes it — optional, defaulting to the Azure Integration Runtime if you leave it out.

One distinction worth repeating, because it trips up nearly everyone early on: the linked service defines how to connect. The dataset, Lesson 9's topic, defines which specific data inside that connection you actually mean. Next: putting all of this to work, connecting to a real Azure Blob Storage account.
